diagram_candidates.kind: two standard tableaux with q-content annotations
diagram_candidates.claim: For shape (2,1) at q=-1 and e=2, the distinct tableaux s=[1 2; 3] and t=[1 3; 2] have equal q-content tuples (0,1,1), so the residues do not separate these tableau labels.
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The counterexample hinges on a small pair of explicitly named tableaux and a collision of their entrywise q-content sequences; a Ferrers-shape display makes the collision immediate.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw the Young diagram of shape (2,1) twice. Label the upper tableau rows [1,2]/[3] and the lower rows [1,3]/[2]. Annotate entries with ordinary contents (0,1,-1) and (0,-1,1), then show both q-content tuples as (0,1,1) at q=-1. Preserve s≠t and avoid suggesting all cells at e≤n fail separation.
diagram_candidates.confidence: source-supported; optional editorial diagram, not a confirmed rendering error

diagram_candidates.kind: 2-by-2 integer matrix switch with energy change
diagram_candidates.claim: A switch subtracts 1 at (i,a),(j,b) and adds 1 at (i,b),(j,a), preserving row and column sums; with γ=t_ia−t_ib−t_ja+t_jb≥2 it changes size by −e(γ−2).
diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The proof uses a concrete local 2-by-2 switch and its row/column margin preservation to connect global core sizes. A compact matrix sketch can show the switch and energy sign without replacing the proof.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show entries (t_ia,t_ib) in row i and (t_ja,t_jb) in row j; arrows indicate −1 at t_ia,t_jb and +1 at t_ib,t_ja. Mark both row sums and both column sums unchanged. Label γ=t_ia−t_ib−t_ja+t_jb, orientation γ≥2, and Δ|κ|=−e(γ−2)≤0; equality occurs at γ=2.
diagram_candidates.confidence: source-supported; optional editorial diagram, not a confirmed rendering error
